intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is caused by homozygous mutation in the MPV17 gene (137960) on chromosome 2p23.3.

checks.claim: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is caused by homozygous mutation in the MPV17 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we describe five additional patients from two unrelated families with sensorimotor axonal neuropathy without hepatocerebral affection caused by homozygous MPV17 variants
checks.explanation: The paper reports that homozygous MPV17 variants cause axonal sensorimotor neuropathy. The CMT2EE label is OMIM nomenclature for this disorder.

checks.claim: The MPV17 gene is located on chromosome 2p23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: The entire coding regions, including intron–exon boundaries, of the POLG (NM_002693), DGUOK (NM_080918) and MPV17 (NM_002437.4) genes were amplified
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature. The paper itself does not state it.

paragraphs.text: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is an autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy that begins in childhood, adolescence, or adulthood. It causes distal weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs, along with distal sensory loss and absent tendon reflexes. Some patients have ragged-red fibers and other mitochondrial abnormalities in muscle. Most reported patients have not had the liver or brain involvement seen in Navajo neurohepatopathy, another disorder caused by MPV17 mutation (Choi et al., 2015; Baumann et al., 2019). However, Blakely et al. (2012) described a patient whose neuropathy was accompanied by leukoencephalopathy and mild liver abnormalities.

checks.claim: CMT2EE is an autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: This study enrolled two autosomal recessive Korean families with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy (FC26 and FC355, Fig. 1a).

checks.claim: CMT2EE begins in childhood, adolescence, or adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: He first developed neurological symptoms at age 14 years, with gradual onset of walking difficulties
checks.explanation: This paper only documents onset in adolescence. Onset in childhood or adulthood is not described here.

checks.claim: CMT2EE causes distal weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: Neurologic examination at the age of 34 years revealed muscle weakness and atrophies of bilateral, distal muscles, predominantly in the lower limbs.

checks.claim: CMT2EE causes distal sensory loss and absent tendon reflexes.
checks.evidence_quote: Vibration and position senses were more severely disturbed than pain and touch senses. Knee and ankle jerks were absent.
checks.explanation: Sensory loss and absent reflexes reported in both patients.

checks.claim: Some patients with CMT2EE have ragged-red fibers and other mitochondrial abnormalities in muscle.
checks.evidence_quote: histochemical analysis demonstrated clear evidence of muscle involvement with ragged red fibres and a mosaic pattern of COX deficiency.
checks.explanation: The patient had ragged-red fibres and other mitochondrial abnormalities in muscle.

checks.claim: Most reported patients with CMT2EE have not had the liver or brain involvement seen in Navajo neurohepatopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: the present two patients showed only axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, and they did not exhibit any liver or brain abnormalities, at the ages of 34 and 22 years.
checks.explanation: Paper reports this for its own two patients only; the generalization to 'most reported patients' is not in this paper.

checks.claim: Navajo neurohepatopathy is another disorder caused by MPV17 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in MPV17 cause mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome 6 (MTDPS6) (NNH; MIM #256810), also known as Navajo neurohepatopathy

checks.evidence_quote: We describe a patient presenting with a severe peripheral neuropathy, leukoencephalopathy and liver involvement due to a homozygous MPV17 gene mutation
checks.explanation: The paper also says there was no significant chronic liver disease, so the liver abnormalities were mild.

paragraphs.text: Blakely et al. (2012) reported a 21-year-old Pakistani man, born to nonconsanguineous parents, who began having difficulty walking at age 14 years. Over several years this progressed to bilateral foot drop requiring orthoses. He had symmetric distal numbness that began in the feet and ascended to the knees, with milder involvement of the hands. On examination he had distal muscle wasting, clawed toes without pes cavus, a slow unsteady gait, and decreased tone. Distal weakness was severe (MRC grade 0/5 in some hand muscles and in the anterior tibialis), and hip flexion was mildly weak. Tendon reflexes were absent and sensation was lost distally in the lower limbs. He had no significant cognitive impairment. Nerve conduction studies showed an axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Sural nerve biopsy showed a severe chronic axonal neuropathy with only occasional surviving myelinated axons. An MRI at age 9 years had been normal, but later cranial MRI showed diffuse T2 hyperintensity in the cerebral white matter and cerebellum, suggesting leukoencephalopathy. CSF protein (1963 mg/L) and lactate (4.3 mmol/L) were increased. He also had mild hepatomegaly, abnormal liver echogenicity, and a minimally raised gamma-GT. Liver biopsy showed patchy steatosis (about 20%) with early bridging fibrosis, although he had no clinically significant chronic liver disease. He had recovered fully from hepatitis A at age 3 years. His sister developed a progressive, fatal hepatitis at age 9 years. Their father had an episode of hepatitis in childhood and recovered fully. The mother and an older brother were well.

paragraphs.text: Choi et al. (2015) reported 2 unrelated Korean patients, each born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents. Patient 1 (family FC26) was a 34-year-old woman whose early motor milestones were normal. She first noticed distal lower limb weakness at age 9 years and began walking with short leg braces at age 12. At age 34 she had distal weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs. Atrophy of the intrinsic hand, foot, and calf muscles was severe. She also had flexion deformities of the interphalangeal joints, ankle deformity, and scoliosis. Vibration and position sense were more affected than pain and touch, and knee and ankle jerks were absent. She had no liver involvement and no other features of Navajo neurohepatopathy, but her serum lactate was mildly raised (2.1 mmol/L). Patient 2 (family FC355) was a 22-year-old man who had had gait and balance problems since age 13 years and began walking with short leg braces at age 20. He had distal weakness and atrophy, atrophy of the intrinsic hand, foot, and calf muscles, and flat feet. Vibration and position sense were more impaired than pain and touch, and deep tendon reflexes were absent. He had no other features of Navajo neurohepatopathy. Apart from a slightly raised serum lactate (1.9 mmol/L), his laboratory results were normal.

paragraphs.text: Electrophysiologic findings were similar in the 2 patients of Choi et al. (2015). Sural sensory nerve action potentials were lost early in the disease, and no sensory responses could be elicited in either patient. Peroneal and tibial CMAPs were absent, and median and ulnar motor conduction velocities and CMAPs were reduced. Visual and brainstem auditory evoked potentials were normal, and brain MRI showed no abnormality. On muscle MRI, the soleus muscles showed severe atrophy and fatty replacement, while the tibialis posterior and lateral gastrocnemius were relatively spared. Thigh and hip muscles were much less affected, a pattern consistent with length-dependent axonal degeneration. The authors noted that the preferential involvement of the soleus resembled CMT2A. Sural nerve biopsy from patient 1 at age 34 showed near-complete loss of large and medium-sized myelinated fibers and atrophy and vesicular changes in unmyelinated axons. There was no demyelination and there were no onion bulbs, consistent with an axonal neuropathy. A vastus lateralis biopsy from patient 2 at age 22 showed a few ragged-red fibers and subsarcolemmal accumulation of enlarged mitochondria.

paragraphs.text: In the patient reported by Blakely et al. (2012), skeletal muscle biopsy showed ragged-red fibers (about 1%) and about 20% COX-deficient fibers in a mosaic pattern. On electron microscopy there were subsarcolemmal abnormal mitochondria with paracrystalline ('parking lot') inclusions. Muscle mtDNA copy number was normal, but long-range PCR showed multiple mtDNA deletions. Single-fiber real-time PCR showed high levels of clonally expanded mtDNA deletions in COX-deficient fibers. The authors noted that multiple mtDNA deletions had not previously been reported in patients with MPV17 mutations.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of CMT2EE in the families reported by Blakely et al. (2012), Choi et al. (2015), and Baumann et al. (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. Choi et al. (2015) described their 2 Korean families as autosomal recessive: in each family the affected individual was homozygous for the MPV17 mutation and was born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents. Blakely et al. (2012) noted that their patient's parents were nonconsanguineous but of the same Asian ethnicity. They suggested that the homozygous mutation pointed either to a shared common ancestor or to a high population prevalence of this recessive mutation in that Asian group, and they considered a common founder most likely.

checks.evidence_quote: revealed a homozygous missense variant (c.2898C>T; p.Pro98Leu) in MPV17 which has previously been reported as a recessive mutation
checks.explanation: For Blakely et al., a homozygous recessive mutation is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. The parts about the other two papers are not addressed here.

paragraphs.text: Blakely et al. (2012) sequenced the POLG, DGUOK, and MPV17 genes in a Pakistani man with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy and leukoencephalopathy. They identified a homozygous missense mutation in MPV17, pro98-to-leu (P98L). The nucleotide change was given as c.2898C-T in the text and as c.298C-T in the figure legend. The affected residue is conserved from human to yeast, and the variant had previously been reported as a recessive mutation associated with mtDNA depletion in liver. Parental samples were not available to confirm carrier status.

paragraphs.text: In 2 affected individuals from 2 unrelated Korean families, Choi et al. (2015) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.122G-A transition in the MPV17 gene. The mutation results in an arg41-to-gln (R41Q) substitution at a conserved residue, and it was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Each parent was presumed to carry 1 mutant allele. The variant was absent from 300 controls, from in-house exome data (n = 302), and from the dbSNP142 and 1000 Genomes databases. It was present at very low frequency in ESP (0.00008) and ExAC (0.00002471). In NSC34 mouse motor neuronal cells, siRNA knockdown of Mpv17 significantly reduced cell proliferation and viability under oxidative stress (H2O2) and affected OXPHOS levels. Overexpressing the R41Q mutant significantly inhibited proliferation.

paragraphs.text: Baumann et al. (2019) studied 2 unrelated families with axonal sensorimotor neuropathy. In the affected members of the first family they found a homozygous R41Q mutation in the MPV17 gene. In the affected members of the second family they found a novel homozygous near-splice variant in MPV17, c.376-9T-G, which they showed caused an in-frame deletion of 11 amino acids. The authors noted that MPV17 mutations were first reported in Navajo neurohepatopathy, an autosomal recessive mtDNA depletion syndrome. They concluded that MPV17 mutations should also be considered in patients with pure, nonsyndromic axonal neuropathy.

paragraphs.text: Choi et al. (2015) noted that previously reported MPV17 patients with neuropathy also had hepatopathy or brain involvement. By contrast, their 2 patients with the homozygous R41Q mutation had only axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, without liver or brain involvement at ages 34 and 22 years. They noted that a different substitution at the same residue (R41W) also impaired proliferation of NSC34 cells, and they suggested that mutations at arg41 predominantly cause peripheral neuropathy.

paragraphs.text: Blakely et al. (2012) studied a 21-year-old Pakistani man, born to nonconsanguineous parents, who had axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, leukoencephalopathy, mild liver abnormalities, and multiple mtDNA deletions in muscle. In this patient they identified a homozygous pro98-to-leu (P98L) mutation in the MPV17 gene. The nucleotide change was reported as c.2898C-T in the text and as c.298C-T in the figure legend. The residue is conserved from human to yeast, and the variant had previously been reported as a recessive mutation associated with mtDNA depletion in liver. Parental samples were not available. Because the parents were of the same Asian ethnicity, the authors considered a common founder most likely.

paragraphs.text: Choi et al. (2015) studied 2 affected individuals from 2 unrelated Korean families who had axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy without liver or brain involvement. Using whole-exome sequencing, they identified a homozygous c.122G-A transition in the MPV17 gene, resulting in an arg41-to-gln (R41Q) substitution at a conserved residue. The mutation was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. It was absent from 300 controls, from 302 in-house exomes, and from the dbSNP142 and 1000 Genomes databases, and it was present at very low frequency in ESP (0.00008) and ExAC (0.00002471). Overexpressing the R41Q mutant in NSC34 mouse motor neuronal cells significantly inhibited cell proliferation.
